grades.quote:
Any file descriptors descended from that same call to `open` share the same open file description. For example, in the previous example of `ls` and `ps` writing to the `information` file, each of the two processes has its own file descriptor, but they are referring to the same open file description, and hence share the same file offset. If a process independently calls `open` on the same file, however, it will get a separate file offset.

A process implicitly increases the file offset whenever it does a `read` or `write` of length more than zero. It can also explicitly change the file offset using the `lseek` procedure.
grades.reason: Explains that inherited descriptors share an offset and that lseek changes that shared position, allowing one process to affect the other.
Mentions xv6 lacking lseek but does not explain file-position sharing after fork.
The fork exercise concerns scheduling and copy-on-write, not shared file positions.

grades.quote: Two file descriptors share an offset if they were derived from the same original file descriptor by a sequence of fork and dup calls. Otherwise file descriptors do not share offsets, even if they resulted from open calls for the same file.
grades.reason: Directly establishes that descriptors inherited through fork share the file position, so seeking through one affects the other.
